answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each identity carry a costly, verifiable signal before it can transact. New agents must lock a refundable stake and complete a proof-of-work attestation tied to a unique device key, like a black onyx seal that cannot be copied cheaply. The stake sits on a ledge: honest agents keep trading and eventually reclaim it, while detected sybils forfeit theirs. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand stakes and a thousand attestations, turning cheap duplication into a linear, expensive cost, while a single honest agent pays only once.
